title: add-robust-tail-triage-and-traffic-smoothing-gate
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: We observed intermittent tail latency spikes during low-to-medium traffic that evade percentile-based detectors and cause noisy rollbacks. This PR introduces two complementary runtime guards: (1) an entropy-weighted tail triage detector that fuses per-cohort latency distributions and token-length conditioned entropy to surface anomalous tail modes, and (2) a traffic-smoothing gate that applies adaptive request shaping and staged traffic slices to reduce amplification when a new rollout exhibits increased variance. The goal is to reduce noisy canary churn while preserving rapid detection of true regressions. Implementation summary: - Add an entropy index (shannon-based) computed on binned per-request latency histograms per tenant/cohort. - Combine entropy index with median/tail ratio signals via a logistic fusion to produce a single anomaly score. - Implement an adaptive slicing controller that ramps traffic into a candidate variant using N progressive slices where slice sizes are chosen based on current cluster headroom and the fused anomaly score. - Provide a fallback fast-fail path: if the fused anomaly score exceeds the emergency threshold, traffic is immediately diverted to the stable variant and an incident alert is fired. Operational notes: - New config under perf.canary.entropy_triage with knobs for bin_size_ms, entropy_window_minutes, tail_ratio_weight, emergency_threshold, and slice_policy. - Default settings are conservative and backwards compatible; the feature is disabled by default and enabled via rollout policy in the Console. Tests and validation: - Extensive unit tests for entropy computation, fusion logic, and controller state transitions. - Integration test that replays production-sampled latencies (sanitized) demonstrating a 42% reduction in noisy rollbacks in a synthetic workload. - Load test run on staging (see CI artifacts) with no measurable throughput regression. Linked artifacts: Linear tickets ENG-2382 (detector design) and ENG-2410 (rollout controller). Related work: builds on prior probe-based canary work (probe orchestrator and cohort samplers) but targets variance-driven false positives rather than mean drift. Checklist: - [x] Detector algorithm implementation - [x] Controller and policy plumbing - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Console UI flags + docs - [x] E2E staging validation - [x] Release notes

notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: feature disabled by default and gated behind Console rollout to allow incremental adoption.
